note: Task 14 (chunk e4): breathing. The functions of breath.html that its README calls normative (the dark's `render`, `sizeCanvases`, `setStyle`; the window's `openWindow`, `windowOpenness`, `windowDone`, `closeWindow`; `updateLoop`, `frame`; her hand's `say`, `fade`, `clearHand`; `heartTick`; the sound's `audioInit`, `noise`, `thump`, `SFX`, `inhaleStart`, `inhaleStop`; the phases `begin`, `exit`, `blackout`, `wake`; `tap`, `press`; the input's `letters`, `typing`, `breatheDown`, `breatheUp`; the state's `fresh`, `push`, `cancelWindows`, `cueMode`, `st`, `L`, the easings and `pick` / `randInt`), its tables (`STYLES`, `REST_OPEN`, `VIEW_OF`) and the kit's (`SHAPES`, `SEAT_BODY`, `squashOf`, `chaikin`, checked by kit/fidelity.json). Module wiring beyond the listed functions (breath.ts header): `performance`, `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `innerWidth` / `innerHeight` and `Math.random` are the module's own (the scene's frame clock, the mount's timers and frames, the scene's size, a xorshift seeded by fnv1a of the scene and the run: no rng draw); `window` is the module's own `{ __forceO }` (the shots' hook); `$` names the instrument's elements in the effects layer (under the scene's UI: the stop word's pill is never covered), the scene's reply, input line and input, and the letters laid over the input; the reply's opacity and the line's width and border are written through claims (styleClaims.ts, recorded as written); the prototype's top-level listeners are the mount's (`env.listen`: Space and T never from a field or a control, the left button only on the frame, preventDefault so the field keeps its focus, any phase as the prototype's; a key-up of Space or a mouse-up releases whichever pressed, as the prototype's; like it, no release on a lost window focus; Enter in the field sends the line as heard; T is TAP's key, the rings live in the effects layer, which is hidden from assistive tech); the grain tile is made per mount. The engine's numbers (BEAT, DRAIN, CAUGHT, MISSED, CRUEL_MISSED, SEAL_RELIEF) are TUNING.physics.breath scaled to the run's capacity (the air is the gauge's share); the air is set from the engine's gauge as each segment starts. `S` is the approved defaults with the run's shape (`occlusionOf` of the contact: kind, side, angle; the kit's `S` is set the same), the view (`ceiling` falls back to `room` when the scene has no ceiling art or it fails to load), her face point (`art.face`) and the still form (`env.reduced`, `env.readable`). Her lines: see `L` (ruling Q: `cardVoice` `breath.*`, checked by `lines`; the model's words of window_open, window_false, greedy and warning may take their place). Playful's 'again.' is played ahead of a planned opening where the gap holds it (see `scheduleWindow`). The prototype's `KINDS` and the rejected `seat_x_*` shapes, the panel, the start overlay, the summary, the debug readout and the `__` hooks are prototype only (`_breath` is the tests' and the shots' hook). Added: the gap of a leaky seal (`gap_breath`, a dashed ring under the TAP ring, glossary `gap_breath`), as the card's button today. CSS (checked by the shots): the prototype's styles under `.alius-breath` (her lines in her hand at its sizes × her hand's measured scale, R10); the narrowed input line keeps a min-width of 420 px, because the scene's line carries its prompt and tools beside the field (the prototype's has neither); her own is sized to its natural size each frame. Her lines wrap inside the frame (max 40 %, and `keepInFrame` moves one back from an edge); the prototype's are short and on one line. The `greedy` row of physicsCues (Task 13) is only the model's fallback for its own call; the hand never writes it.

differences.reason: Prototype only (README: the rhythm scheduler): the openings, their widths and the false ones are the engine's plan (`effectiveOpenings`, placed per running segment on the loop's clock), so `isFalse` is the plan's flag. Playful's 'again.' (review I5) is the prototype's branch, played ahead of the planned opening: "three… two… again." at `T − 3c … T − c` with nothing opening, then, 200 ms later, the prototype's new window scheduled `k·BEAT` on (k 1–2), which is the planned opening on its own beat (T = at − 200 − k·BEAT); it is played only when the whole count fits after the previous opening (`opts.after`), and never otherwise. A count step that would fall before now is skipped instead of firing at once. The window's beat is read from its queue entry's time as it fires (so her delay, which moves the entry, moves its beat), a window still open is closed first, and an opening that came due during the entry plays as the loop begins on its own beat (a late event of the prototype's queue fires at once; review I3); its width (`R.widthMs`, read by `st()`) and her lines for that beat (`refreshLines`) are set as it opens; a silent opening is the plan's (no cue on its beat: R4) as well as `cues: none`.

Wiring: the opening is reported to the engine as it closes (`reportWindow`: a `breathe` with the share held, `credit / CAUGHT`, or a false window reached for). Prototype only: the end after `S.len` windows (the engine ends the hold) and the next window's scheduling (the plan has them).
Wiring: no audio context yet is not an error (`A.ctx &&`). Prototype only: the summary and wake cards (P15a's wake card follows the scene) and the stand-in reply (the scene's reply is the model's).
